guitar.notes: Steppenwolf's guitarists used standard Gibson gear of the late 60s; no singularly iconic instrument is well documented, low confidence.

tone.target: fuzzy 60s psych rock crunch with wah-like bite
tone.profile: fuzzy 60s psych rock crunch with wah-like bite
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Boost (Wah) -> Distortion -> Amp (UK 45) -> Cab (UK Vintage 4x12) -> EQ -> Delay -> Reverb.

rig.name: Steppenwolf - Magic Carpet Ride - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from fuzz and high gain stages.
Provides the required wah-like bite and mid-range boost for vocal articulation.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here primarily for its V-Wah function, simulating a dedicated wah pedal effect before the main fuzz/distortion chain.

blocks.purpose: Creates the core fuzzy texture and vintage psych rock grit.
Adds extra mid-bite and punch to cut through the mix without sounding like generic overdrive.
blocks.gap: Using a dedicated Boost for subtle, focused mid-range lift rather than relying solely on the fuzz/wah.

blocks.purpose: Simulates the classic Plexi/Marshall edge tone required for 60s psych rock.
Provides the classic British cabinet sound associated with this genre.
Fine-tune the tone by emphasizing mids and controlling low end bloat.
Adds a subtle sense of space and echo characteristic of psych rock.
Adds necessary ambience without the heavy wash of plate or spring reverb.
blocks.gap: The verdict specifically asked to 'drop heavy reverb', so Room is chosen over Plate/Spring for a more controlled, natural decay.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the raw, punchy sound of 60s psych rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, punchy character needed for 60s psych rock.
